members.claim: This migration also changes the primary keys of all three tables (RateLimitConfig, RateLimitCounter and RateLimitEntry) from AutoField to BigAutoField. That is unrelated to the token-bucket fix. On PostgreSQL and MySQL it rewrites each table while holding an exclusive lock, and RateLimitEntry can be very large because it stores one row per request for sliding windows. Running `migrate` during an upgrade could block rate-limited traffic for a long time. Nothing in the changelog or upgrade notes mentions this, and the PR describes the change as a simple added column. Split the PK changes into a separate, documented migration (or leave them out) so the fix migration only adds the column.

members.claim: The RenameIndex operations are only added when the installed Django version has RenameIndex (4.1+). The project also supports Django 3.2 and 4.0, so the result of this migration depends on which Django version applies it. On 3.2/4.0 the index names stay as they were in 0001, while on 4.1+ they are renamed. When those users later upgrade Django, the old names will no longer match the model, and `makemigrations --check` will report pending changes or create unwanted migrations. Shipped migrations should be deterministic. Either drop the renames from this bug-fix migration or give the indexes explicit `name=` values in models.py so they always match.

findings.claim: The catch-all except still lets the request through on schema errors, so a missing migration silently disables rate limiting.
findings.evidence: The root cause of #24 was that every exception is caught and the request is allowed. A missing column raised a DB error, which was logged and then the request was allowed with a full bucket, so rate limiting silently stopped working. This PR fixes the schema but leaves that path unchanged. Users who upgrade and forget to run the migration will again silently have no rate limiting. At minimum, schema errors (e.g. ProgrammingError/OperationalError) should be raised or reported clearly, not treated as fail-open.
